cards.explanation: The one reason the text gives is that she was a virgin. Amnon, one of King David's sons, was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar “…for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.” I think this is a spot to slow down, friends. Trouble is brewing in Amnon before anything has happened.

Jonadab asks Amnon why he looks so down. Jonadab, Amnon's friend, says, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” He's noticed Amnon is low day after day, and he asks about it straight. The text calls Jonadab a very shrewd man, so keep an eye on what he does with the answer.

The answer is True. Amnon answers Jonadab, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.” Absalom is another son of King David. Amnon doesn't dodge the question, he just says it. Remember that Jonadab is called a very shrewd man.

Jonadab says Amnon should ask for Tamar to come and make him food. He tells Amnon to say to his father, “Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.” That's the plan, and it starts with pretending to be ill. I think this is where the shrewdness is going.

The answer is True. King David sends word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.” That's his message to her, and it comes after Amnon asked the king for this while pretending to be ill. The text doesn't say more about what David knew, so I'll leave it there.

The answer is False. Tamar brings the pan and sets it down before Amnon, but he refused to eat. Then he says, “Send everyone away!” Notice that he asked for the food and then wouldn't touch it. I think that tells us the cakes were never the point.
What Amnon orders is, “Send everyone away!” He refuses to eat, and then the text says everyone went out. Now Tamar is alone with him. I think this is where we all hold our breath.

The word is bedroom. Amnon says, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.” Tamar takes the cakes she made and goes to her brother Amnon's bedroom. I think this is the part where we all want to warn her. Hold on, friends.

The word is Israel. Tamar cries out, “No, my brother! Do not violate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!” She says no, clearly, and she says it more than once. Let's hear her, friends.

She warns him he would be like one of the fools. Tamar says to Amnon, “Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel!” She is speaking up for herself and warning him in the same breath. I think she's brave to say it.

The answer is True. Tamar says, “Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.” She keeps pleading with Amnon and doesn't stop. The text doesn't explain more about what she meant, so I'll leave that open. Notice that she is still trying to stop him.

What Amnon feels is hatred greater than his love before. The text says, “Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had.” His feelings flipped. Then he says to her, “Get up!” and “Be gone!” I think this is a hard line to read.

The answer is False. She doesn't go quietly. After Amnon says “Get up!” and “Be gone!” she answers, “No,” and tells him that “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” She keeps speaking up. I think that's courage, friends.

The word is worse. Tamar says, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” She won't pretend this is small. Then the text says Amnon refused to listen to her. I think her words deserve to be heard.
He tells his attendant to throw her out and bolt the door. Amnon says, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!” Notice he doesn't even call her by name. I think that stings.

She puts ashes on her head and tears her robe. The text says Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. Then she put her hand on her head and went away crying aloud. I think the whole kitchen would go quiet for this one.

The answer is False. Absalom, her brother, says, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” He tells her to be quiet, not to go to the king. I think that's a heavy thing to be told.

The name is Absalom. The text says, “So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.” That's where she is after Absalom speaks to her. I think this verse carries a lot of sorrow.
The answer is True. The text says, “When King David heard all this, he was furious.” That's how the passage puts it. About what David does next, this passage says nothing, so I'll leave it there.

The reason is that he hated Amnon for violating Tamar. The text says Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, “…because he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar.” Absalom stays silent, but the hatred is there. I think that's a warning sign, friends.
